verifyRequiredConsumerSet accepted both results on 2026-10-02, 12 verified cases each; the exact command and its output are in inventory promotion_evidence.t01_06.current_rerun.consumer_set. The verifier does check each result's conformance_pack.byte_sha256 against the pack bytes and the case observations. It does not bind the consumer commit: any 40 lowercase hex commit_sha is accepted, a zeroed one included (consumer_set.binding_limits), so 'exact' holds for the pack bytes and the replayed cases, not for the commit. The beval result was produced by calling replayIdentityConformanceBytes on a checkout, not from the installed tarball. No consumer-set result is bound in evidence-manifest.json, which has no entries.

becoder: the smoke script packs both repositories, installs both tarballs and replays 12/12. beval: npm run test:pack installs backend-evaluator-0.1.0.tgz and replays 12/12 without backend-skeleton installed. Both were run on 2026-10-02 in checkouts at the heads recorded in the inventory. The 'exact repository SHAs' part rests on the commit read from each checkout (becoder --consumer-commit or git rev-parse HEAD; beval git rev-parse HEAD): neither script checks that the working tree is clean, and nothing ties the commit in a result to the replayed bytes.

current_state.requirements_note: MET_BY_RERUN means the checks named in the basis were re-run on 2026-10-02 and passed. MET_BY_RERUN_COMMIT_NOT_BOUND means the same, and in addition the consumer commit named in the result is not tied to the bytes that were replayed (inventory promotion_evidence.t01_06.current_rerun.consumer_set.binding_limits). NOT_LOCATED means the search named in the basis found nothing. PARTLY means part of the requirement is met. In the consumer results, execution.exit_code, execution.bskel_runtime_imported and execution.bskel_runtime_spawned are constants written by the result builders (becoder lib/next/identity-consumer-result.mjs lines 91 to 93, beval lib/next-runtime/identity-consumer.mjs lines 163 to 165), not observations. The line 'bskel runtime import/spawn both false' in consumer_result_contract.guarantees_checked below is the wording of 2026-09-25; what the verifier checks is that a result says false there. The line 'consumer repository and exact commit' in the same list is also the wording of 2026-09-25; what the result verifier checks is that the repository is a non-empty string (verifyRequiredConsumerSet also matches the repository names against the required list) and that the commit is 40 lowercase hex characters; it does not check that the commit exists or is the one that produced the result. MET_BY_RERUN_COMMIT_NOT_BOUND is attached only to items 3 and 4, whose requirement text asks for 'exact consumer results' (item 3) and 'exact repository SHAs' (item 4); items 1 and 2 ask only that the reader replays the pack and emits a result, so they keep MET_BY_RERUN although their basis also says that the commit named in the result is not tied to the code that produced it.
